questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha (Society for Welfare of the Ostracized)?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Dr. BR Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. BR Ambedkar** was the founder of the **Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha**, established in the year **1924**.
 
• The main aim of the Sabha was to promote the **welfare and upliftment of the ostracized sections** of society, particularly the **Dalits**.
 
• The Sabha worked to **spread education** and awareness among the oppressed classes and to provide them with **equal rights**.
 
• It was one of the key organizations formed by Dr. Ambedkar to fight against **social discrimination** and advocate for the **abolition of untouchability**.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar, a prominent social reformer and the architect of the **Indian Constitution**, dedicated his life to the cause of achieving **social justice** for marginalized communities.
 
• He believed that education was the most powerful tool for empowerment and worked relentlessly to bring **educational and social reforms** through initiatives like the Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad**__

 __
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** was the first **President of India**.
 
• He was a prominent leader in the **Indian independence movement** and a key figure in the formation of the Indian Constitution.
 
• He was associated with the **Indian National Congress** and played a major role in the **freedom struggle**.
 
• While he made significant contributions to the nation, he was not connected with the establishment of the **Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha**.
 
 
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore**__
 __
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** was a renowned poet, philosopher, and the first non-European to win the **Nobel Prize in Literature** in **1913**.
 
• He is best known for his literary works, including **Gitanjali**, and for composing the national anthems of **India** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• Though Tagore was a social reformer, he was not involved in the formation of the **Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha**.
 
 
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang**__
 
 
• **Atmaram Pandurang** was a social reformer and one of the founders of the **Prarthana Samaj** in **1867**.
 
• The Prarthana Samaj was aimed at promoting **religious and social reforms** within Hindu society.
 
• While his contributions to social reform are noteworthy, he was not associated with the establishment of the **Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha**.

questions.question: The office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India falls under which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ministry of Home Affairs**__.

__
 
• The **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India** operates under the jurisdiction of the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
• This office is responsible for conducting the **decennial Census of India**, which is one of the largest administrative exercises in the world.
 
• The office was established under the provisions of the **Census Act, 1948**, a law enacted to regulate the census process in India.
 
• The Registrar General and Census Commissioner is also tasked with maintaining the **National Population Register (NPR)**.
 
• The Census provides critical **data and statistics** that help in policy formulation and implementation across various sectors, including education, health, housing, and employment.
 
• The office plays a significant role in gathering demographic, socio-economic, and cultural data which is vital for **nation-building** and planning.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** ensures coordination and supervision of this office's activities to achieve accuracy and efficiency in census operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Ministry of Rural Development**__

 __
 
• The **Ministry of Rural Development** is responsible for promoting rural infrastructure, livelihood, and development programs in India.
 
• It oversees schemes such as the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)**, and **National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)**.
 
• This ministry focuses on addressing poverty and improving the living standards of people in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Finance**__
 __
 
• The **Ministry of Finance** is responsible for managing the financial system of India, including the preparation and presentation of the **Union Budget**.
 
• It oversees departments like **Revenue, Expenditure, Economic Affairs**, and **Financial Services**.
 
• The ministry plays a key role in taxation, fiscal policy, and regulation of financial institutions.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**__
 
 
• The **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** is responsible for formulating and implementing health-related policies in India.
 
• It oversees programs related to **public health**, **medical education**, and **family welfare.**
 
• The ministry manages initiatives like **Ayushman Bharat**, **National Health Mission (NHM)**, and **Universal Immunization Program (UIP).**

• The promotion to Super 750 level signifies the growing prominence of Indian badminton on the **international stage**.
 
• Higher-level tournaments like Super 750 attract more **world-class players**, offer larger prize money, and enhance the visibility of the sport in the host country.
 
• This decision reflects the **efforts of the Badminton Association of India** (BAI) in organizing and promoting the sport effectively.

questions.question: To whom is the Orange Cap awarded in the Indian Premier League (IPL)?

• Introduced in the **inaugural season of IPL in 2008**, the Orange Cap symbolizes the batting excellence of a player throughout the league.
 
• The player who has scored the most runs wears the Orange Cap on the field during matches, and the final holder of the cap is announced at the end of the season.
 
• If two or more players score the same number of runs, the award is given to the player with the **higher strike rate.**
 
• Some notable players who have won the Orange Cap include **Chris Gayle, David Warner, Virat Kohli, and KL Rahul.**
 
• The Orange Cap is an incentive for players to perform consistently and contribute significantly to their team’s performance.
 
• This recognition enhances the profile of the winning player and demonstrates their role as a key contributor to the league.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The youngest players in IPL history, such as **Prayas Ray Barman** and **Noor Ahmad**, have gained significant attention for their skills and potential.
 
 
 
• **Emerging player of the league**__
 __
 
• This award is given to a young player who has shown exceptional talent and promise during the tournament.
 
• Criteria for this award include being under the age of **25**, having played fewer than **five Test matches**, and not having been part of more than **two IPL seasons.**

questions.question: What was the goal of 'National Beekeeping & Honey Mission' ('NBHM')?

options.text: To achieve the goal of the 'Black Revolution'
To achieve the goal of the 'Sweet Revolution'
To achieve the goal of the 'Red Revolution'
To achieve the goal of the 'Pink Revolution'

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To achieve the goal of the 'Sweet Revolution'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (NBHM)** was initiated to promote the development of scientific beekeeping in India.
 
• The primary objective of the NBHM is to achieve the goal of the **'Sweet Revolution'**, which aims to increase the production of **honey and related products**.
 
• The 'Sweet Revolution' is a government initiative launched to promote **apiculture** or beekeeping as part of a sustainable agricultural strategy.
 
• Beekeeping plays a vital role in increasing the **pollination efficiency** of crops, leading to higher yields and contributing to the growth of the **agriculture and horticulture sectors**.
 
• The mission provides financial assistance and technical guidance to farmers and beekeepers to enhance their **beekeeping practices**.
 
• It also emphasizes the production of quality honey and other bee-related products to meet **domestic and international market demand**.
 
• NBHM is implemented under the Ministry of **Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare** in collaboration with the **National Bee Board (NBB)**.
 
• It promotes cross-sectoral collaboration for research and innovation in **honeybee health, breeding, and management**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **'Black Revolution'**__

 __
 
• The 'Black Revolution' refers to the efforts aimed at increasing the production of **petroleum and related products**.
 
• It focuses on reducing the dependency on **imported crude oil** through indigenous production strategies.
 
 
 
• **'Red Revolution'**__
 __
 
• The 'Red Revolution' is associated with the increase in the production of **meat and tomato**.
 
• It is focused on enhancing **food security** and improving **nutrition levels**.
 
 
 
• **'Pink Revolution'**__
 
 
• The 'Pink Revolution' is related to the growth in the production of **poultry and shrimp**.
 
• This initiative aims to boost the **livelihoods of farmers** and meet the rising demand for **poultry products**.

questions.question: What was the proposed status of RGNIYD (Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development)?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Deemed National Youth University**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Development (RGNIYD)** is an institute established by the Government of India in **1993.**
 
• It is located in **Sri Perumbudur, Tamil Nadu.**
 
• RGNIYD was granted the status of a **Deemed University** under Section 3 of the **University Grants Commission (UGC) Act, 1956.**
 
• The institute serves as a vital resource center for **youth-related activities, policies, and programs.**
 
• It offers **academic programs**, training, and research in areas related to **youth empowerment and development.**
 
• RGNIYD collaborates with various **national and international organizations** to promote youth development.
 
• The institute focuses on areas such as **skill development, leadership training, and social entrepreneurship** to empower young individuals.
 
• It is dedicated to studying and addressing issues related to **youth in India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Youth Organisation**__

 __
 
• An **International Youth Organisation** typically refers to global bodies focused on youth development, such as **UNESCO's youth programs** or **World Youth Alliance.**
 
• These organizations aim to address issues affecting youth worldwide, such as **education, health, and employment.**
 
• RGNIYD is not designated as an international organization but rather focuses on the **Indian youth demographic.**
 
 
 
• **Central University**__
 __
 
• A **Central University** is established by an Act of Parliament in India and is directly funded by the **Government of India.**
 
• Examples include **Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU)** and **Delhi University.**
 
• While RGNIYD has the status of a **Deemed University**, it is not categorized as a Central University.
 
 
 
• **Regional Youth Development Centre**__
 
 
• A **Regional Youth Development Centre** typically operates at a local or regional level to address specific youth issues within a region.
 
• RGNIYD functions as a **national-level institute**, making it distinct from a regional center.

questions.question: What is the name of the southern half of the Pangaea supercontinent that existed about 300 million years ago?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gondwana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gondwana** was the name given to the **southern half** of the supercontinent **Pangaea**, which existed approximately **300 million years ago**.
 
• The term "Gondwana" is derived from the **Gondwana region in central India**, where some of the earliest geological studies were conducted.
 
• It included modern-day landmasses such as **South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia, and the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• **Gondwana's breakup** began around **180 million years ago**, leading to the formation of the continents we see today.
 
• The geological evidence supporting the existence of Gondwana includes **similar fossil records**, such as the presence of **Glossopteris flora**, across these continents.
 
• Gondwana played a critical role in the study of **plate tectonics** and the understanding of continental drift.
 
• The fragmentation of Gondwana contributed to **major biodiversity changes** and the distribution of species across different continents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rodinia**__

 __
 
• **Rodinia** was a supercontinent that existed around **1.3 to 0.9 billion years ago**, much earlier than Gondwana.
 
• It is significant in the study of **Precambrian geology**.
 
• Rodinia eventually broke apart, leading to the formation of subsequent supercontinents, including **Pannotia** and later **Pangaea**.
 
 
 
• **Pannotia**__
 __
 
• **Pannotia** was a transient supercontinent that existed approximately **600 million years ago**.
 
• It formed after Rodinia but existed for a relatively short period before breaking into Gondwana and other land masses.
 
• Pannotia is less studied compared to Gondwana and Rodinia due to limited geological evidence.
 
 
 
• **Nuna**__
 
 
• **Nuna**, also known as the **Columbia supercontinent**, existed around **1.8 to 1.5 billion years ago**.
 
• It is one of the earliest known supercontinents and was significant in the **Proterozoic era**.
 
• Its breakup contributed to subsequent continental formations and the evolution of Earth's geology.

questions.question: Mayiladumparai, which was notified in 2022 as the oldest Iron Age site in the Indian subcontinent, is in which of the following states in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mayiladumparai** is located in the state of **Tamil Nadu**, India.
 
• It was notified in **2022** as the **oldest Iron Age site** in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Recent excavations at Mayiladumparai have unearthed evidence of **Iron usage dating back to 2172 BCE**, making it one of the earliest sites of Iron Age activity in India.
 
• The findings indicate that Tamil Nadu had a **well-established Iron Age culture** much earlier than previously thought.
 
• Mayiladumparai is significant for understanding the **transition from the Neolithic to the Iron Age** in southern India.
 
• These discoveries are important for tracing the **development of metallurgy** and its impact on social and economic structures in ancient Tamil Nadu.
 
• The excavations were conducted under the supervision of the **Department of Archaeology, Tamil Nadu.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maharashtra**__

 __
 
• Maharashtra is home to several prominent archaeological sites, including the **Ajanta and Ellora Caves**, which are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
 
• The state is also known for its **Satavahana dynasty**, which contributed significantly to trade and culture in ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Kerala**__
 __
 
• Kerala has a rich history of trade and cultural exchanges, especially through its **port of Muziris**, which was a hub for international trade during ancient times.
 
• The state is famous for its **Neolithic rock engravings** found in Edakkal caves.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**__
 
 
• Karnataka is known for its **Hampi**, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The state also has significant Iron Age sites such as **Hirebenakal**, known for megalithic structures.

questions.question: In which Part of the Indian Constitution are Directive Principles of State Policy enumerated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IV**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are enshrined in **Part IV of the Indian Constitution**, covering Articles **36 to 51**.
 
• The Directive Principles serve as **guidelines** to the central and state governments of India for formulating policies and enacting laws.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by a court of law, but they are **fundamental in the governance** of the country.
 
• The DPSPs aim to establish a **welfare state** by addressing social and economic disparities and promoting justice, equality, and liberty.
 
• The idea of DPSPs was borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**, which in turn was influenced by the **Directive Principles of Social Policy** in the Irish context.
 
• Some key principles include ensuring **equal pay for equal work**, promoting the **right to education**, and securing a **living wage** for workers.
 
• The DPSPs also cover areas such as **promotion of international peace and security, protection of the environment, and organization of village panchayats**.
 
• The Directive Principles complement the **Fundamental Rights (Part III)**, and together they form the conscience of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Part III**__

 __
 
• **Part III** of the Indian Constitution deals with **Fundamental Rights**, which are guaranteed to all citizens of India.
 
• It includes Articles **12 to 35** and provides rights such as the **Right to Equality**, **Right to Freedom**, and **Right to Constitutional Remedies**.
 
• Unlike DPSPs, Fundamental Rights are **justiciable**, meaning they can be enforced by the courts.
 
 
 
• **Part V**__
 __
 
• **Part V** of the Constitution pertains to the **Union Government** of India.
 
• It includes provisions related to the **President, Vice President, Council of Ministers, and the Parliament**.
 
• It also outlines the **legislative, executive, and judicial powers** of the Union.
 
 
 
• **Part II**__
 
 
• **Part II** of the Constitution deals with **citizenship** and includes Articles **5 to 11**.
 
• It defines who is considered a **citizen of India** at the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• It also provides for the **acquisition and termination of citizenship**.

questions.question: Which revolution followed the Green Revolution in India, focusing on increasing the production of fruits and vegetables?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Golden Revolution**__.

__
 
• The **Golden Revolution** in India refers to the period when significant emphasis was placed on increasing the production of **fruits, vegetables, honey, and horticultural crops**.
 
• This revolution was crucial for enhancing **agricultural diversification** and boosting the economy through **horticultural advancements**.
 
• The term is associated with the time frame between the **1991–2003** due to focused policies and investments in horticulture.
 
• It played a vital role in improving the **quality of nutrition** and food security in the country.
 
• The revolution was driven by the efforts of **agricultural scientists, government initiatives, and collaboration with farmers**.
 
• Horticulture crops like fruits, vegetables, flowers, nuts, spices, and honey witnessed remarkable growth during this period.
 
• The **National Horticulture Mission (NHM)**, launched in 2005, further accelerated the benefits of the Golden Revolution.
 
• This revolution contributed to the enhancement of **income generation** for farmers by promoting high-value crops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **White Revolution**__

 __
 
• The **White Revolution** refers to the period of increased milk production in India, making the country the largest producer of milk in the world.
 
• This revolution was spearheaded by **Dr. Verghese Kurien**, known as the 'Father of the White Revolution'.
 
• The **Operation Flood program**, launched in 1970 by the **National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)**, played a pivotal role.
 
• It helped in achieving self-sufficiency in dairy production and improved the livelihood of millions of rural farmers.
 
 
 
• **Blue Revolution**__
 __
 
• The **Blue Revolution** is associated with the growth of **aquaculture and fisheries** in India.
 
• It focused on enhancing fish production and sustainable management of aquatic resources.
 
• The revolution contributed significantly to **food security and employment generation** in coastal regions.
 
• Government schemes like the **National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB)** have supported this initiative.
 
 
 
• **Yellow Revolution**__
 
 
• The **Yellow Revolution** refers to the increase in the production of **oilseeds** in India.
 
• This revolution was aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in edible oil production.
 
• It was primarily driven by the **Technology Mission on Oilseeds**, launched in 1986.
 
• The focus was on crops like **mustard, sunflower, and soybean**.

questions.question: If a fish eats a shrimp, the energy gets transferred from:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**primary consumer to secondary consumer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The energy transfer in a food chain occurs from one trophic level to another. Here, the **fish** is a secondary consumer, and the **shrimp** is a primary consumer.
 
• A **primary consumer** feeds directly on producers (like plants or algae). Shrimps feed on algae, making them primary consumers.
 
• A **secondary consumer** feeds on primary consumers. In this case, the fish eats the shrimp, so the energy gets transferred from the shrimp (primary consumer) to the fish (secondary consumer).
 
• This relationship is part of the **energy flow in an ecosystem**, where energy decreases as it moves up the trophic levels due to loss as heat and metabolic processes.
 
• The concept is explained by the **10% energy rule**, where only about 10% of the energy is transferred to the next trophic level, while the rest is lost.
 
• This flow of energy is vital for maintaining the **balance of ecosystems** and ensuring survival at various levels of the food chain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Producer to decomposer**__

 __
 
• Producers, such as plants or algae, are at the **base of the food chain** and convert sunlight into energy through **photosynthesis.**
 
• Decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, break down dead organisms and recycle nutrients back into the soil. There is no direct energy transfer from producers to decomposers in the context of the given question.
 
 
 
• **Secondary consumer to primary consumer**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because energy transfer does not occur **backward** in a food chain. Secondary consumers cannot transfer energy to primary consumers.
 
 
 
• **Secondary consumer to tertiary consumer**__
 
 
• This option refers to energy transfer from a secondary consumer to a tertiary consumer (e.g., a hawk eating a fish). However, in this scenario, the shrimp is not a tertiary consumer, making this option irrelevant.
